note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

nodes.name: Pairwise LLM EM ignores set structure
nodes.description: Most LLM-based entity matching judges each (anchor, candidate) pair in isolation, ignoring interactions among candidates and the clean-clean constraint that at most one candidate matches.

nodes.name: Fixed pipelines ignore difficulty and cost
nodes.description: Manually designed composite pipelines such as COMEM apply the same operator sequence to every anchor regardless of difficulty, so inference cost is a fixed byproduct of the architecture, and cost matters at industrial scale.

nodes.name: Cost-aware sequential MDP formulation
nodes.description: Multi-candidate EM with blocking is cast as an episodic MDP per anchor, where actions invoke operators that update candidate scores and accumulate abstract cost until DECIDE or Tmax.

nodes.name: Four operators
nodes.description: The controller chooses among MATCH (pairwise, lightweight Flan-T5-xl), COMPARE (champion vs challenger preference), SELECT (listwise choice over top-k shortlist) and terminal DECIDE(i)/DECIDE(None), each with a model capacity.

nodes.name: Abstract two-level cost model
nodes.description: Operators carry a low/high cost label (high = rho x low, rho=2.5 by default), a relative control signal that decouples the policy from any specific pricing or model.

nodes.name: Reward and state design
nodes.description: The state concatenates scores, candidate masks, COMPARE frequency, global context (cost, time, max score) and action history; rewards combine terminal correctness, a cost penalty and potential-based shaping on the score margin Phi.

nodes.name: PPO-trained MLP policy
nodes.description: The policy is a 3-layer MLP (768-384-192) trained with PPO and a learned value baseline, trained once on the AB dataset.

nodes.name: Backend-agnostic controller
nodes.description: Because the controller sees only abstract operators and cost labels, stronger LLMs can be plugged in at inference without retraining as long as operator interfaces and relative cost levels hold.

nodes.name: Competitive with supervised DITTO at low cost
nodes.description: Zero-shot on other datasets CaRL-EM averages F1macro 76.09 versus 85.64 for in-domain DITTO (about 89%) at 5.9% of DITTO's cost.

nodes.name: Beats COMEM at far lower cost
nodes.description: CaRL-EM beats the strongest hand-crafted baseline COMEM on average F1macro with about 4.5x cost reduction, and with the same GPT-4o mini backend uses only 22% of COMEM's total cost, forming a new Pareto frontier.

nodes.name: Better abstention on no-match
nodes.description: CaRL-EM stops with a no-match decision more readily when evidence is weak, giving higher F1none than the fixed pipeline (e.g. 68.20 vs 60.78), which avoids false positives.

nodes.name: Transfers zero-shot and across backends
nodes.description: DITTO trained on AB drops from 85.64 to 59.75 F1macro on other datasets, while CaRL-EM stays high; swapping backends without retraining usually raises F1macro and cost, with the controller adjusting MATCH/COMPARE usage.

nodes.name: Adaptive operator use and position robustness
nodes.description: CaRL-EM uses fewer MATCH/COMPARE calls than COMEM, varies steps with dataset difficulty (more on AG, WA), and is more stable across gold-candidate positions than baselines.

nodes.name: Ablation: cost term
nodes.description: Removing the cost term leaves F1macro unchanged (76.07) but raises cost by about 15%.

nodes.name: Ablation: operators matter
nodes.description: Removing MATCH drops F1macro to 65.87 (F1none 49.86), removing COMPARE to 73.69, removing SELECT to 73.26 (cheapest but lower F1id).

nodes.name: Ablation: potential shaping
nodes.description: Removing the potential-based term Phi lowers F1id and F1macro (75.93) and makes performance less stable (Std 14.56 vs 12.24).

structural_reasoning: Limitations of pairwise and fixed-pipeline EM motivate the MDP formulation; operators, cost model, state/reward and policy training lead to the performance, transfer, behavior and ablation results.
